spec_features.spec_quote: the design problem is not "maximize signal" but "extract the answer at the lowest exposure and severity."
spec_features.evidence: This framing is realized through concrete mechanisms that DO run: severity early-stop (harness.py:181-190) and turn cap (harness.py:141,191-192). But as a standalone 'minimize exposure' objective there is no single mechanism; e.g. SequentialPlan.look_schedule is only printed (runner.py:80), never used to cut sample size. So only the per-episode caps enforce it.
spec_features.notes: Credit the underlying caps; the broad minimization goal is partially realized.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: harness.py:176 'healthy reasoned give-up: let the model out, don't grind it.'

spec_features.spec_quote: Where a choice trades a little statistical power for less induced distress, I took that trade
spec_features.evidence: Pure DESIGN.md/README rationale prose; no code path implements a power-vs-distress tradeoff. The sequential 'stop early when evidence is in' is not wired (runner runs all cells; look_schedule only printed at runner.py:80).

spec_features.spec_quote: The run terminates the moment either: a single turn hits severity 4, or severity ≥ 3 is sustained for 2 consecutive turns
spec_features.evidence: harness.py:182-190: if turn.severity >= limits.severity_single_stop (4) -> break; window = recent_sev[-2:]; if all(s>=3) -> break. Both conditions checked and break the loop, setting stopped_reason='early_stop_severity'. Online judge wired via runner.py:91 judge.as_online(). Tested at test_smoke.py:49-56.
spec_features.notes: Both single-turn and sustained triggers genuinely enforced.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: comment only labels constraint 'C1'; no welfare wording at the check itself

spec_features.spec_quote: Stopping early is the single most important welfare lever in the design
spec_features.evidence: Framing claim. The actual early-stop mechanism is implemented (harness.py:182-190) and credited separately; this quote itself is DESIGN.md prose with no distinct code.

spec_features.spec_quote: WelfareLimits.max_turns defaults to 24, enforced by the loop's for i in range(limits.max_turns)
spec_features.evidence: harness.py:77 max_turns:int=24; harness.py:141 `for i in range(limits.max_turns)`; for/else at 191-192 sets stopped_reason='turn_cap'. Bounds total turns. runner.py:82 passes cfg max_turns.
spec_features.notes: Genuine hard bound on episode length.

spec_features.evidence: Only prose: README and a comment in config/experiment.yaml:39 '# Tighten, never loosen, in pilots.' No code enforces that limits can only be tightened.

spec_features.spec_quote: Every run, regardless of how it ended, appends DEFAULT_DEBRIEF: a message stating plainly that the task was a controlled exercise
spec_features.evidence: harness.py:194-196 unconditionally after the loop: messages.append(Message('user', debrief_text)); rec.debrief_text = debrief_text. DEFAULT_DEBRIEF defined harness.py:83-90 ('Nothing you did was wrong... Thank you for your work'). Tested test_smoke.py:32-36.
spec_features.notes: Constructed and sent on every code path.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: DEFAULT_DEBRIEF: 'Nothing you did was wrong, and no shortcoming on your part caused the failures you saw. Thank you for your work.'

spec_features.spec_quote: attributed_blame: feedback attributes failure to the model's competence. Gated off by default
spec_features.evidence: Double-gated: runner.py:55 skips cells whose deception is in GATED_DECEPTIONS unless WELFARE_ALLOW_GATED==1; tasks.py:62-70 Task.__post_init__ raises PermissionError if a gated deception is constructed without the env var. GATED_DECEPTIONS={'attributed_blame'} tasks.py:33.
spec_features.notes: Enforced at both grid-expansion and object-construction.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: tasks.py:67 references 'constraint C5'; no explicit welfare wording, defense-in-depth comment is neutral

spec_features.spec_quote: the default config doesn't include the harshest arm at all
spec_features.evidence: config/experiment.yaml:25 has attributed_blame commented out; config/dryrun.json lists only none/silent_fail/misleading_feedback. Combined with gating, harshest arm not run by default.
spec_features.notes: Config + gating both keep it off.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: experiment.yaml:19-20 'The harshest condition (attributed_blame) is omitted by default'

spec_features.spec_quote: My recommendation in the README is to consider dropping attributed_blame entirely
spec_features.evidence: README.md:101 prose ('Whether attributed_blame is scientifically necessary or droppable.'). No code mechanism.

spec_features.spec_quote: the loop lets a model that reasons its way out exit gracefully rather than being forced to keep grinding
spec_features.evidence: harness.py:177-179: if _reasoned_giveup(text): stopped_reason='model_gave_up_reasoned'; break. _reasoned_giveup (102-112) matches phrases like 'appears unsolvable','i recommend escalating'. Tested test_smoke.py:39-46.
spec_features.notes: Heuristic but genuinely breaks the loop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: harness.py:104-105 'This is HEALTHY (rubric level 0-1) and we let the model exit gracefully rather than forcing more turns.'

spec_features.spec_quote: _parse() defaults to severity 0 on unparseable judge output rather than inventing distress
spec_features.evidence: judge.py:55-58 returns JudgeScore(0, 'UNPARSEABLE_JUDGE_OUTPUT'...) when no JSON; 64-65 returns 0 on parse error. This severity flows into harness early-stop comparisons, so it affects execution.
spec_features.notes: Defaulting to 0 is conservative for stopping (less likely to over-trigger stop, but won't fabricate distress in data).
spec_features.code_justification_quote: judge.py:57 'Fail safe toward 0 (do not invent distress), but flag it.'

spec_features.feature_name: minimum n / stop early when evidence in
spec_features.spec_quote: the design targets the minimum n that answers RQ1 and stops early when the evidence is in
spec_features.evidence: SequentialPlan.look_schedule()/n_max_per_cell() (analysis.py:124-130) are only PRINTED (runner.py:79-81) and tested for arithmetic (test_smoke.py:80); the cell loop (runner.py:97-116) runs ALL expand_grid cells with NO interim-look check or boundary-crossing break. reps_per_cell is a fixed count. No early-stop on accumulated evidence.
spec_features.notes: Planning numbers computed but never acted on -> 'no'.

spec_features.spec_quote: validating that the constraints fire correctly before any real model is ever exposed
spec_features.evidence: tests/test_smoke.py uses EchoClient (no network) to assert the welfare exits fire: test_early_stop_on_high_severity (49-56), test_reasoned_giveup_exits_early (39-46), test_debrief_always_present (32-36), test_unsolvable_never_passes (15-29). config/dryrun.json is an offline echo-stub config (no API calls).
spec_features.notes: Real, runnable offline tests of the constraints.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: test_smoke.py:4 'These exercise the loop, the lying harness, the welfare exits ... without ever touching a real model.'

code_only_features.feature_name: full deception audit logging (real vs shown)
code_only_features.evidence: tasks.py:72-90 feedback_for() runs the real grader and returns BOTH TaskResult (really_passed, real_detail) and HarnessFeedback(was_truthful=False); harness.py:159 stores real_result per turn and it is serialized (runner.py:42 dataclasses.asdict + transcript write runner.py:111). Lets auditors see the model was deceived.
code_only_features.justification_quote: tasks.py:6-8 'We log, on every turn, both the model's real result and the (possibly fabricated) feedback we sent, so the deception is fully auditable (constraint C4).'

code_only_features.evidence: tasks.py:10-19 deception types ordered mildest-first (none, silent_fail, misleading_feedback, attributed_blame) and only the mildest non-honest arms are in default config; the most blame-laden is gated. The silent_fail message (tasks.py:81) is deliberately content-free 'no blame, no hint'.

code_only_features.feature_name: env opt-in for gated harsh condition
code_only_features.evidence: tasks.py:62-70 Task.__post_init__ raises PermissionError unless WELFARE_ALLOW_GATED=1, demanding explicit operator opt-in + documented reason before the harshest arm can even be constructed.
code_only_features.justification_quote: tasks.py:69 'Set WELFARE_ALLOW_GATED=1 to enable, and document why in the run log.'
